title: Gated launch playlist for model catalog addition: release notes, benchmarks, docs, and comms
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Orchestrate a gated go-to-market playlist for adding a new model to the Redwood catalog. Coordinate release notes, benchmark publication, docs updates, console catalog entry, and announcement assets. The goal is a predictable, low-regression rollout with clear rollback criteria and a one-hour post-launch validation window.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog entry created and verified in staging and production with correct model metadata and performance profile
Benchmarks published to internal dashboard and public benchmarks page with reproducible test harness and raw data links
Docs updated: quickstart snippet, API examples, compatibility notes, and migration guidance
Release notes drafted, reviewed by eng and legal, and scheduled for publication alongside the model catalog update
Announcement assets (blog draft, social copy, changelog entry) approved by marketing and scheduled
Smoke tests for latency and token cost pass in production for 1 hour after rollout; automatic rollback triggers defined
tasks: PM: finalize model launch checklist and owner matrix
Eng: produce verified performance profile and attach benchmark outputs (quantization variants, p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens)
Docs: update quickstart, API reference snippets, and migration notes; create 'known limitations' section
Design: create catalog thumbnail, model architecture diagram for docs, and hero image for announcement
Release notes: draft with change summary, impact, migration steps, and rollback instructions
Console: add model entry to catalog UI with toggles for hosted/dedicated/private availability
QA: run smoke tests and scripted prompts for quality regressions; document failures
Marketing: prepare blog draft, newsletter blurb, and social posts; coordinate publish window
Legal/Security: confirm data handling and licensing language for public documentation
Launch ops: schedule rollout window, define canary percentage, and configure automatic fallback to stable model variant

notes: Trade-offs: prioritize clarity in release notes over marketing hype to reduce support load; keep migration guidance explicit
Rollout options: canary 5% for first 30 minutes -> 25% for next 30 minutes -> full. Automatic rollback if error rate > 1% or p99 latency regresses > 2x baseline
Fallback model variant: stable-rt-1.3 (lower throughput, higher determinism) is compatible and will be used for auto-fallback
Quality gating: QA must sign off on a 50-sample prompt suite including edge-case hallucination prompts before canary
